ideas.title: Deep-Dives index group jump-nav
ideas.problem: The Deep-Dives index is a single scrollable page with 75+ entries across 12 groups and no anchor jump-nav at the top. A reader who wants 'Safety & Security' must scroll past 30+ entries (Architectures, Protocols, Memory, RAG) to reach it. The section will only grow, compounding the problem.
ideas.proposal: Add a sticky-within-page group anchor bar at the top of the Deep-Dives index (below the hero): one pill/badge per group linking to its `<div id>` anchor. The group headers in SectionIndexView already render as `.toc-part-label` divs — add `id` attributes keyed by group slug and render the anchor bar from the same `groups` array. No manifest schema change needed.
ideas.evidence: SectionIndexView.astro renders `groups.map(g => <div class='toc-part'>...)` with no `id` attributes. NAVIGATION-PLAN.md §2 P4 flagged this at 51 entries; the worktree now has 75 entries across 12 groups (counted from `src/content/deep-dives/groups/*.ts`). The live page at https://agentic-ai-wiki.vercel.app/deep-dives confirms no jump-nav exists.
open_questions: Should the same jump-nav appear on the Concepts index (only 4 groups — lower urgency but nice consistency)?
Sticky within-page vs static — does sticky conflict with the sticky site-header at 56px?
ideas.mockup_hint: Draw the Deep-Dives index page. Below the hero lede, before the first group, show a horizontally-scrolling strip of small uppercase badges (JetBrains Mono, 10px, matching .side-part style) — one per group: 'Architectures & Patterns', 'Protocols & Interop', etc. Each badge is a link; clicking scrolls to that group header. On mobile the strip is horizontally scrollable. The currently-visible group badge could get the accent underline as you scroll.

ideas.title: Mobile prev/next nav on section detail pages
ideas.problem: On screens ≤900px the `.chapter-side` sidebar is hidden entirely (CSS: `display:none`) and replaced with a single 'Browse all X →' back-link. This means mobile readers have no way to navigate to the adjacent entry — no prev/next, no sibling context. The prev/next buttons that exist at the bottom of every detail page are the only escape route, and they are invisible until the reader reaches the very end of a long article.
ideas.proposal: Add a compact prev/next strip immediately after the `.mobile-section-nav` back-link (which already exists and is shown only on mobile). The strip uses the same prev/next data already computed in SectionEntryLayout.astro (`prev` and `next` variables). It requires no new data: just two short `<a>` tags with ← / → arrows and the sibling title, styled to fit in a single line at small viewport.
ideas.evidence: site.css line 86-90: `@media (max-width: 900px) { .chapter-side { display:none; } .mobile-section-nav { display: block; } }`. SectionEntryLayout.astro lines 34-36 already compute `prev` and `next`. The bottom `.page-nav` already renders them — it's just too far away on mobile after a long article.
competitor_examples: MDN Web Docs mobile prev/next at article top
open_questions: Should the same top prev/next strip be added to the Field Guide's ChapterLayout as well?
Title truncation: deep-dive titles can be long (e.g. 'ReAct — Interleaving Reasoning and Acting') — use ellipsis or shorten to just the first clause?
ideas.mockup_hint: Draw a mobile viewport (375px wide) of a Concepts or Deep-Dives detail page. Just below the 'Browse all Concepts →' back-link, show a two-column row: left cell has '← prev' in muted mono caps and the previous entry's title in Fraunces serif (truncated with ellipsis if needed); right cell has 'next →' and the next title, right-aligned. The row is separated from the back-link by a thin rule. Keep the existing bottom .page-nav buttons as-is.

ideas.title: Reading-path callout on Concepts and Deep-Dives index pages
ideas.problem: A newcomer landing on /concepts or /deep-dives sees a flat list of grouped entries with no recommended entry point, no sense of which entries to read first, and no pointer to the Field Guide as the structured path. The Concepts tagline ('plain-language entries for newcomers and intermediates') promises orientation but the page delivers none.
ideas.proposal: Add a small 'New here?' callout block between the hero and the entry list in SectionIndexView. For Concepts: suggest a five-entry core path (what-is-an-llm → what-is-an-agent → the-agent-loop → tool-calling-explained → what-is-rag) as a horizontal chip list with a 'or follow the guided Field Guide →' escape. For Deep-Dives: a one-liner 'These essays assume Concepts fluency — new? Start with Concepts →'. All copy lives in `src/i18n/ui.ts` (bilingual). SectionIndexView receives an optional `readingPathHtml` prop from the section-specific view.
ideas.evidence: NAVIGATION-PLAN.md §2 P1 (unshipped). HomeView.astro already links Concepts with its tagline but never names an entry point. The Concepts tagline in ui.ts says 'newcomers and intermediates' but the index gives no path. Five-entry core path is already named in NAVIGATION-PLAN.md §2 P1.
open_questions: Should the five-entry Concepts path be rendered as a mini horizontal chip-list or as a simple prose sentence?
Does the zh translation need a different core-path sentence or is it a straight translation of the en text?
ideas.mockup_hint: Draw the Concepts index page. Between the page hero (h1 + lede) and the first group ('AI Foundations'), insert a bordered callout box (using the existing .callout.tip CSS style — green 'TIP' badge). Inside: 'New to agentic AI? Read these five entries in order:' followed by five pill-links in a wrapping flex row (what-is-an-llm, what-is-an-agent, the-agent-loop, tool-calling-explained, what-is-rag), then a small muted line 'Or follow the full guided path in the Field Guide →'. Show the equivalent Deep-Dives callout in a second artboard: simpler, just one sentence 'These essays go deep — new here? Start with Concepts →'.

ideas.title: Add Home to all breadcrumb trails
ideas.problem: Breadcrumbs on detail pages show `[Section] / Group / Entry` — e.g. `Concepts / Agentic AI / What Is an AI Agent?` — but no site-root 'Home' link. The Field Guide breadcrumb in ChapterLayout shows `[Field Guide] / Part / Chapter`. A reader who deep-links to a detail page from search has no breadcrumb escape to the site root, only to the section index.
ideas.proposal: Prepend a `Home` link (localised: '首页' in zh) to all three breadcrumb variants: Field Guide, Concepts, and Deep-Dives. In SectionEntryLayout.astro (line 72), change the `.breadcrumb` div to start with `{locale === 'zh' ? '首页' : 'Home'} /` before the existing section link. Same change in ChapterLayout.astro (line 27). Add the `home.breadcrumb` string to `UIStrings` in ui.ts for clean i18n.
ideas.evidence:
SectionEntryLayout.astro line 72-73: `
{rootLabel} / {groupNm ? ...}`. ChapterLayout.astro line 27: same pattern. Live at https://agentic-ai-wiki.vercel.app/concepts/what-is-an-agent the breadcrumb reads 'Concepts / Agentic AI / What Is an AI Agent?' — no Home. Standard web practice and WCAG 2.4.8 (Location) best-practice.
competitor_examples: tailwindcss.com docs breadcrumb always starts with home icon
open_questions: Use the word 'Home' / '首页' or a house icon? Icon avoids language but needs an alt attribute.
Should the site brand in the header also carry aria-label='Home' for redundancy?
ideas.mockup_hint: Draw the breadcrumb strip from a Concepts detail page in two states: before (Concepts / Agentic AI / What Is an AI Agent?) and after (Home / Concepts / Agentic AI / What Is an AI Agent?). Use the existing .breadcrumb CSS — JetBrains Mono 11px uppercase muted text, accent-ink on hover. Show the zh version below: 首页 / 概念 / 智能体 AI / 什么是 AI 智能体？

ideas.title: Scope Deep-Dives sidebar to current group
ideas.problem: The sidebar on a Deep-Dives detail page renders all 75 entries across all 12 groups. This is an extremely long, dense list that overwhelms the sidebar's navigational value — the active entry is buried somewhere in the middle. The reader cannot tell at a glance which group they are in or how many peers it has.
ideas.proposal: In DeepDiveLayout.astro (or SectionEntryLayout via a new `sidebarMode` prop), pass only the current group's entries to SectionSidebar, plus a compact 'group switcher' above the list: a small collapsible or static list of all group names where the current group is expanded and highlighted. The group name becomes a heading in the sidebar. A small '↑ All groups' link at the bottom of the sidebar returns to the Deep-Dives index. This keeps the sidebar scannable (6-9 entries instead of 75) while preserving cross-group navigation.
ideas.evidence: DeepDiveLayout.astro passes `groups={groupedEntries(locale)}` (all 75 entries, 12 groups) to SectionEntryLayout, which passes it unchanged to SectionSidebar. At 75 entries the sidebar is already impractical; NAVIGATION-PLAN.md §1 pain point #6 and §2 P4 flag this. The react-pattern detail page live fetch confirmed the sidebar lists all groups and many entries.
open_questions: Should Concepts sidebar also be scoped (4 groups, 33 entries — less urgent but consistent)?
For the group switcher: static list (simpler, no JS, accessible) or CSS-only accordion? Static is lower risk.
Does scoping the sidebar break the bilingual parity requirement? (No — group names are already localised in the manifest.)
ideas.mockup_hint: Draw two sidebar states side by side. Left (current): a very long list of all 12 group headings each with many entries, active entry barely visible. Right (proposed): a short group switcher at the top showing all 12 group names as small mono uppercase links, with 'Architectures & Patterns' highlighted in accent color. Below it, an expanded list of only the 8 entries in that group, the active one accented. At the bottom a small '← All Deep-Dives' link. The total sidebar height is 1/8 the current. Show the same on a 375px mobile viewport — the sidebar is still hidden, but the 'Browse all' link now also says the group name: 'Browse Deep-Dives: Architectures & Patterns'.

ideas.title: Field Guide prev/next label legibility
ideas.problem: The Field Guide prev/next navigation buttons render labels like '0·4 Async Python' and 'I·1 The Loop', where '0' is the roman numeral for Foundations (confusingly numeric rather than symbolic), '·' is a centered dot separator, and the chapter number is an integer parsed from a zero-padded string. On small screens this dense mono label is hard to parse at a glance, and the '0' for Foundations is not intuitive.
ideas.proposal: Change the prev/next label format in ChapterLayout.astro (line 16) from `{partRoman}·{parseInt(num)} {title}` to a two-line format: a small line with the part name (e.g. 'Foundations') in muted mono, and the chapter title on the main line in Fraunces serif. Rename the Foundations roman from '0' to 'F' (or '·') in the manifest, or special-case it in the label function. This matches the `.page-nav-btn .dir` / `.title` structure that already exists in guide.css.
ideas.evidence: ChapterLayout.astro line 16: `const label = (c: typeof ch) => \`${c.partRoman}·${parseInt(c.num, 10)} ${c.title[locale]}\``. The Foundations part has `roman: '0'` in field-guide/manifest.ts line 21. The `.page-nav-btn` already has `.dir` (small label) and `.title` (large Fraunces) divs — the current code passes a single string to `.title`, wasting the two-tier structure. The field guide renders prev/next as a single flat string rather than using the dir+title split.
competitor_examples: css-tricks.com chapter nav (part name above, title below)
open_questions: Renaming Foundations roman from '0' to 'F' or 'Foundations' changes the ChapterSidebar too — verify the sidebar roman display looks right.
Should the part name in the prev/next label match the sidebar part name exactly, or use a shorter abbreviation?
ideas.mockup_hint: Draw two versions of the prev/next footer bar from a Field Guide chapter page. Left (current): two big dark buttons, each showing a single string like '← 0·4 Async Python' in one line of Fraunces italic. Right (proposed): the same two buttons, but each shows a small muted mono top line ('← FOUNDATIONS') and below it the chapter title in larger Fraunces italic ('Async Python'). The .dir div carries the part name and arrow; the .title div carries just the chapter title. Show one cross-part transition: left button 'FOUNDATIONS / Async Python', right button 'BUILD / The Loop'.

notes: Potential overlaps with other lenses: ux-ia-03 (reading-path callout) may overlap with a content or onboarding lens; ux-ia-05 (sidebar scoping) may overlap with a performance or CSS lens. Ideas considered and dropped: (1) Locale switcher position — the EN/中文 switcher is far right after search, which is standard and functional; the zh parity check found no issues. Not proposing a move. (2) Skip-link — already present in BaseLayout.astro line 45 (`.skip-link`). Not re-proposing. (3) SectionIndexView inline styles — many styles are inlined rather than in CSS classes; this is a code quality issue, not a UX/IA issue, so dropped. (4) Anchor links within long deep-dive articles — out of scope for this lens (content, not IA). The five ideas ux-ia-01 through ux-ia-05 map directly to the un-shipped P1/P3/P4 proposals in NAVIGATION-PLAN.md but with concrete implementation detail and fresh evidence from the live site. ux-ia-06 is a net-new finding not mentioned in NAVIGATION-PLAN.md.
